Following the Lumentum / Marvell deal: 

My opinion is that independent Western laser players, like $AAOI, $COHR, and $SIVE became a lot more strategically valuable. 

$MTSI and $SMTC should get some attention too as emerging laser players in 2027. 

If I had to guess: 

1. Companies competing against Marvell, or not in the $NVDA ecosystem bandwagon, such as $AMD, are likely going to rethink their relationship with $LITE.

If getting bottlenecked by Nvidia capacity agreements wasn't enough... Incentives around qualifying + bringing up other laser players, seems very necessary now. 

Since you generally don't want competitors like Marvell to have influence or visibility over your roadmaps, IP, capacity, pricing, etc. even if there is a "firewall".  

2. $MRVL acquiring Lumentum opened pandoras box in a way of acquiring a critical chokepoint all your competitors + buyers use. 

$LITE was used by your major hyperscalers and across AI supply chains. 

Now, your leaders might wonder if weaponizing capacity agreements might not be as effective.... If someone else can just buy the entire company. 

There's only a few major public merchant Western players out there, and I'm also sure many others will want to follow the Marvell / Broadcom route via vertical integration, given I think $MRVL saves around $1B+ in costs/year. 

So M&A premiums likely went up. 

$SMTC was actively looking to buy laser capacity via M&A so I'm sure they're looking at $SIVE given their 100M CW DFB laser expansion + tiny MC. 

$JBL also probably wants to vertically integrate down the road too so $SIVE is also an acquisition target for their 1.6T program. 

$AMD was looking for ELSFP + CW capacity given Nvidia bottlenecks, so I'm sure they've looked at $AAOI. 

can go on and on about other ASIC players (like in Taiwan) that likely are looking at vertical integration too.

Since multiple players use a small subset of laser suppliers, if competitors just go ahead and buys them... 

There's a lot pressure to M&A for their own supply chain defensibility. 

TLDR: Independent laser suppliers should capture a material strategic revaluation since $MRVL + $LITE, sets a new precedent + implications. 

We'll see what happens.

South Korean tech outlet The Elec has published a follow-up report on Terafab with some interesting details. Here are the key takeaways:

- ACM Research is looking to supply panel-level packaging equipment to Terafab. Although the company generates 99% of its revenue in China, it has also been an Intel supplier. With an Intel veteran now overseeing Terafab, much of Terafab’s supplier base is similar to Intel’s. The project is moving forward with a 700 × 700 mm panel format.

- Terafab is reportedly working with Samsung as well as Intel and TSMC. The partnership is not exclusive to Intel.

- Micron reportedly declined to participate in Terafab.

- Intel is working with Terafab because it sees the company as a customer rather than a competitor. Intel has yet to secure external foundry customers, so it lacks customer references. It needs to put its technology into actual customer products, refine it, and build confidence in its reliability. In that sense, collaborating with Terafab could be a significant opportunity for Intel.

- Industry sources have been impressed by Terafab’s drive. The impression is that the team is serious about the project and determined to make it happen, whatever it takes.

- SK hynix will eventually end up working with Terafab as well.

- Fabs across Texas are reportedly losing substantial numbers of employees to Terafab, with Tesla seen as the most desirable employer in the state. Many employees have left NXP and Samsung for Terafab, and Samsung has been filling those vacancies by hiring from its suppliers, creating a ripple effect of talent losses across the supply chain.

我对短期半导体仍然偏空。

把 Oracle、GOOG 和 INTC 的暴跌放在一起看，核心问题不是 AI 故事还能讲多久，而是 AI 资本开支的增长速度正在放缓。

市场现在也开始更重视两件事：公司手里到底有没有现金，以及它们能不能顺利融资。

第一，AI Capex 不一定马上见顶，但增长速度已经放慢。

AI Capex，指的是公司为了发展人工智能而投入的钱，比如购买 GPU、建设数据中心和升级服务器。

只要资本开支的增长速度变慢，市场就会开始担心：AI 投入还能增长多久？这些投入什么时候才能赚回来？

即使公司投入的钱还在增加，只要市场开始讨论“高峰”“上限”和“回本时间”，芯片公司的订单增长和估值都可能受到压力。

简单来说，投入继续增加，不代表半导体股还能像以前一样快速上涨。

第二，GOOG 和 INTC 的暴跌，击穿了传统的 GEX Wall 防线。

GEX Wall 可以理解为一个重要的期权支撑位。

当市场接近这个位置时，做市商通常需要进行对冲交易。过去，很多人认为这种对冲交易可以减少短线波动，帮助股价守住关键位置。

但 GEX Wall 不是绝对安全的支撑。

如果公司基本面变差、资金开始流出，同时市场波动率上升，GEX Wall 也可能被击穿。

一旦关键价位失守，做市商的对冲交易可能不再帮助股价稳定，反而可能变成顺势卖出，进一步放大下跌。

这就像一堵墙被撞破后，原本的防守位置可能变成下跌加速点。市场会重新寻找下一个支撑区间，半导体板块的波动也可能明显加大。

第三，Oracle 已经给资本开支安排了高峰。

Oracle 管理层预计，FY27 到 FY28 会是资本开支高峰，FY29 开始下降。

这不一定说明整个 AI Capex 已经见顶，但至少说明资本开支不可能永远保持越来越快的增长。

市场通常不会等到资本开支真的下降后才反应，而是会提前交易这个预期。

如果股价仍然按照“投入会持续加速”来定价，但客户已经开始关注投资回报，那么上游芯片公司的估值迟早会受到压力。

AI Capex 即使继续增加，也不代表半导体股还能维持原来的上涨速度。

反弹可以交易，但目前还没有足够证据证明趋势已经反转。

接下来我只看三点：

1. 公司的现金流有没有改善；
2. 融资是否顺利；
3. 利好消息公布后，股价能不能上涨，并且守住涨幅。
